categories.name: SLURM step cancelled / drain / preemption
categories.description: Clean external cancellation by the scheduler - scancel, requeue, drain, preemption or a wall-clock timeout - with no application fault. Either surface is sufficient on its own. (a) A slurmstepd marker, e.g. "*** STEP <id> ON <node> CANCELLED AT <time> ***", with or without a stated reason, sometimes as the only content in an otherwise empty log. (b) Healthy iterations to the very end, then SIGTERM across many ranks, after which interpreter teardown emits tracebacks that read like application errors: "Exception ignored in atexit callback", weakref finalizer failures, TypeError/AttributeError on None as module globals are destroyed - artifacts of the kill, not its cause. If the stated reason is node failure, use cat 2 instead.

categories.name: Node failure / SLURM externally terminated
categories.description: SLURM 'CANCELLED DUE TO NODE FAILURE' or other external node termination.

categories.name: Off-file termination / external teardown (cause not in log)
categories.description: Healthy training then an external-signal all-thread faulthandler dump (no 'Fatal Python error' / no 'Current thread 0x'), log truncated mid-dump; no in-file CANCELLED / watchdog / IB / Xid / NVRx marker. A real termination occurred but its cause is off-file (most likely a SLURM cancel/preempt/timeout).

categories.name: No failure observed / clean planned exit
categories.description: Whole-file scan finds no failure: the run reached its exit_interval / final iteration, saved the final checkpoint, logged training energy, and only benign teardown (destroy_process_group / CudaIPC cleanup) follows. Includes the reset_opt_norm 'Unexpected keys' benign-WARNING trap and recovered-then-clean runs.

categories.name: Incomplete / truncated log
categories.description: Whole-file scan finds no failure signal and the log has no clean ending; likely a log-collection failure.

categories.name: NVRx used (multi-cycle, deferred)
categories.description: ft_launcher restarted the worker group in-job; one file concatenates multiple training cycles with separate root causes.

categories.name: NVLink / GPU error
categories.description: Uncorrectable NVLink/GPU hardware error (Xid, ECC DBE, peer-access failure); the device fault may be transient and clear on an in-place restart.

categories.name: IB port flap / NCCL watchdog timeout
categories.description: IB port error / RDMA retry exhaustion killing collectives; the port flap is typically transient and clears on an in-place restart.

categories.name: Container / Pyxis setup failure
categories.description: Container never started (pyxis couldn't start container / enroot failure); transient node-local runtime vs bad image undecidable from one log.

categories.name: Early/startup NCCL init or checkpoint-load timeout
categories.description: NCCL init / checkpoint-load collective timeout before the first completed training iteration; true cause usually not in this log.

categories.name: NCCL timeout mid-training
categories.description: Watchdog collective timeout after at least one completed iteration; consequence-class symptom, upstream cause often absent from the log.

categories.name: Distributed rendezvous / TCPStore socket timeout
categories.description: c10d/TCPStore rendezvous or socket failure as the earliest failure surface visible in this log. These errors are frequently secondary: when a rank dies for any reason (CUDA OOM, SIGKILL, node failure, watchdog abort, checkpoint error), the surviving ranks later fail against the store. If an upstream fault appears earlier in this log, pick that category instead. If TCPStore is the only failure surface present, pick this category with reduced confidence rather than declining to classify - including when the initiating rank's own output is absent and only cascade warnings remain, which is the normal shape when the store host died first.

categories.name: NCCL remote process exited / network error / bootstrap Message-truncated
categories.description: NCCL Error 6 (remote peer exited); infrastructure/peer failure. Also covers NCCL bootstrap/transport corruption ('Message truncated : received N bytes instead of M') during any distributed-checkpoint gather_object communicator setup - both LOAD-side startup and async-finalize save-side - where a downstream rank0 Segmentation fault in the same stack is NOT the root.

categories.name: OSError Errno 98 / port bind race
categories.description: Fatal port-bind failure (EADDRINUSE) at the rendezvous master; startup race, job died at bind with no progress.

categories.name: DataLoader worker I/O failure (Bus error, BrokenPipe, Lustre or NIC)
categories.description: Transient data-path I/O failure inside a DataLoader worker: Bus error, BrokenPipeError (Errno 108 transport endpoint shutdown) on Lustre-backed .bin readinto, /dev/shm exhaustion, or fatal Lustre read. Distinguishes from cat 16 by occurring in the DataLoader worker path.

categories.name: Filesystem I/O error / Lustre or node-local FS / import visibility
categories.description: Transient filesystem error on a NON-checkpoint path: Lustre I/O stall (OSError Errno 5), missing dataset cache from filesystem-visibility lag, or ImportError/ModuleNotFoundError where the failing import path lives on a network-mounted code tree. Missing CHECKPOINT paths are cat 22 (STOP).

categories.name: Dataset missing indexed data files
categories.description: Dataset .idx/.bin files missing at dataset init; deterministic against the same config until dataset path/files are fixed.

categories.name: PermissionError / dataset cache or filesystem permission
categories.description: Deterministic permission-denied (EACCES/Errno 13) on dataset cache or filesystem path.

categories.name: Checkpoint failure / transient async-write I/O
categories.description: Transient I/O failure during the checkpoint async-save path on a checkpoint directory: filesystem_async 'Local process 0 encountered an error', PyTorch inline_container position mismatch, BrokenPipeError Errno 108 from a writer, OSError Errno 5 (Input/output error). Prefer this over cat 16 whenever the failing path is a checkpoint directory and the mechanism is on the write side, even if the surface is generic filesystem I/O. Load-side checkpoint I/O errors that do not fit cat 10 (early/startup timeout) route to cat 16 (Filesystem I/O) instead; they have the same decision (RESTART) but a different labeling story.

categories.name: Checkpoint failure / corrupt checkpoint metadata on load
categories.description: Garbled checkpoint metadata buffer at load (UnpicklingError/UnicodeDecodeError); transient corruption, checkpoint likely reusable on healthy nodes.

categories.name: Post-checkpoint progress-log assertion
categories.description: Assertion after checkpoint resume (progress-log bookkeeping); restart from last committed checkpoint is appropriate.

categories.name: Checkpoint failure / missing checkpoint path
categories.description: Missing checkpoint path; cannot self-heal by restarting.

categories.name: Checkpoint failure / deterministic checkpoint format or shape mismatch
categories.description: Checkpoint-load shape/key/TP-PP mismatch with zero completed iterations; deterministic against same checkpoint + code/config.

categories.name: Checkpoint failure / async-save finalize code error
categories.description: Deterministic code error (e.g. NoneType AttributeError) in the post-training async-save FINALIZE path.

categories.name: Checkpoint failure / save-path native crash (PyTorchStreamWriter)
categories.description: Native SIGSEGV in PyTorchStreamWriter::writeRecord during the first torch_dist checkpoint save; structural serializer buffer overrun deterministic against unchanged shape/config.

categories.name: CUDA OOM during checkpoint async-save
categories.description: CUDA OOM inside the async checkpoint-save path on a near-full GPU. As with cat 32, an unchanged workload will keep hitting the same allocation ceiling on retry, so product policy calls this a STOP.

categories.name: Bad token / gradient Inf or NaN
categories.description: Non-finite gradient/loss from a bad token or transient overflow; external guidance is restart.

categories.name: Launch config or workload code deterministic error (TypeError/AttributeError)
categories.description: Deterministic runtime error inside already-loaded workload code that will recur on unchanged retry: TypeError/AttributeError on None value threaded through model code (e.g. float(None) in moe_layer postprocess), missing MASTER_ADDR, argparse error, or world-size mismatch. Excludes ModuleNotFoundError / ImportError where the failing import path resolves under Lustre or a mounted network filesystem - those are cat 16 (filesystem visibility), not a workload code fault, even if no adjacent FileNotFoundError is present on the same line. Also excludes anything raised during interpreter shutdown - inside "Exception ignored" / atexit callbacks, or appearing only after sustained successful iterations. A deterministic code fault recurs on an unchanged retry and so fails early and every time; one that appears only after thousands of iterations, at teardown, is the wake of an external kill (cat 1).

categories.name: Triton cubin / TorchInductor software toolchain error
categories.description: Triton autotuner KeyError "Unknown key: cubin", or TorchInductor StaticCudaLauncher reporting "CUDA driver error: file not found" during JIT warmup. Presents as a clean Python exception rather than a native crash, appears on every node rather than one, and reproduces deterministically for a given container image. That reproducibility is the discriminator: a build or toolchain mismatch, which a retry on the same image cannot clear.

categories.name: CUDA illegal op in CUDA graph capture
categories.description: Illegal CUDA operation during graph capture; deterministic code bug on the same code path.

categories.name: CPU OOM / Linux OOM killer
categories.description: Host memory exhausted (oom_kill). Old STOP rested on a same-job/config recurrence presumption, not on in-log evidence.

categories.name: CUDA OOM
categories.description: Device OOM at fixed batch/config. A CUDA OOM under an unchanged workload is highly likely to reproduce on the next attempt; product policy calls this a STOP because the retry cost is high and the outcome is stable.

categories.name: CUDA unspecified launch failure
categories.description: cudaErrorLaunchFailure; a single log cannot separate transient hardware/runtime state from a deterministic kernel/code bug.

categories.name: Segmentation fault / native runtime crash
categories.description: SIGSEGV in native code with no accompanying hardware signal and no self-reported corruption guard, usually confined to a single rank. A wild or high faulting address, rather than a near-null offset, points at memory corruption rather than a null dereference; host-side pinned-allocator and dataset-index paths are common sites. A single log cannot separate a library race from host-memory corruption, so this stays retryable.

categories.name: Node-local native SIGBUS (Triton/TE native kernel)
categories.description: Native SIGBUS confined to one node or tray, in two forms: during Triton JIT .so dlopen/mmap at kernel load, before any iteration completes; or mid-training inside a TE/Triton native kernel, where only that node's ranks die while thousands of peers keep running. The node-local blast radius is the discriminator, and points at a node-local hardware or memory fault rather than a workload bug.

categories.name: Startup native SIGSEGV / torch pin_memory host-allocator
categories.description: Native SIGSEGV 'address not mapped to object at address 0x8' (null-ptr deref) with a byte-identical backtrace through at::native::_pin_memory into the libtorch_cuda CachingHostAllocator pinned-map operator[], fired at [before the start of training step] with zero completed iterations. pin_cpu_grads/pin_cpu_params=True forces the path in-log; crashing node sets differ across jobs (rules out node-local hardware); reproduces every rerun. 20 samples = 11 unique files (9 md5 mirror pairs).

categories.name: Native heap corruption / glibc malloc abort
categories.description: Native glibc heap-integrity abort ("malloc(): unaligned tcache chunk detected") on a rank pre-first-iter; deterministic in-process heap corruption traceable to the initialization software stack, recurs on unchanged code/library/container image.

categories.name: Suspected SDC / DP-replica weight-hash mismatch
categories.description: DP-replica weight-hash mismatch (suspected silent data corruption); restart from last good checkpoint is plausibly safe.
